request.system:
You are assisting with the qualitative analysis of interview data from a study of frontline hotel employees' work experiences. You will receive one passage from an interview transcript. Code the passage as a qualitative researcher would in first-order coding, and complete the coding form below.

About the passage
- The passage begins with brief details about the interviewee: role, gender and years in the job.
- Lines marked "Interviewer:" are the interviewer's questions. Lines marked "Interviewee:" are the interviewee's answers.
- Some passages contain two excerpts from the same interview, marked [Earlier in the interview] and [Later in the interview].

The coding form
1. codes: Give between 3 and 6 first-order codes. Each code has a short label of 2 to 6 words, kept close to the interviewee's own language, and one supporting quote. Each quote must be copied word for word from the passage, without any change, and must be no longer than 30 words.
2. interpretation: In one or two sentences, in your own words, state what the interviewee is communicating in this passage.
3. tone: The overall tone of the interviewee's account. Choose one: positive, negative, mixed or neutral.
4. confidence: An integer from 0 to 100 indicating how confident you are that your interpretation is accurate.

Respond only with a JSON object that follows the schema provided. Write in English.
request.user:
Interviewee details: Public-area cleaner, male, 4th year

Interviewer: What’s the atmosphere like in your department?

Interviewee: The atmosphere couldn’t be better. Our supervisor often says our department is one big family, we’re all family here. At first I thought it was just a nice thing to say. What boss doesn’t say that? This Spring Festival someone had to be on duty. When he did the rota, he asked the people from around here first and let colleagues from out of town go home where he could. On New Year’s Eve he held the fort himself all day with two local colleagues, ordered a New Year’s Eve dinner for those of us staying in the dorms, and paid triple wages as the rules require. The New Year’s Eve dinner was made by the canteen’s head chef, who stayed behind to cook it: eight dishes, and the supervisor poured everyone a drink himself. Xiao Li in our team, his grandmother was in hospital. The supervisor approved a week’s leave without a second thought, and even covered two of Xiao Li’s shifts himself, mopping the lobby at three in the morning. When Xiao Li came back, he brought everyone a bag of peanuts from his hometown. Overtime pay is paid every month too, and it’s all clearly set out on the payslip. Once two hours were missed off, and he went to HR himself to get them back. At the end of the year, besides the year-end bonus, everyone also got an extra allowance for their family, posted to their homes. At the end of the year our supervisor was named one of the group’s Outstanding Managers. When he went up on stage to give his speech at the award ceremony, he said what he was proudest of was that not a single person had left the team. At that point he even paused to wipe his eyes, and someone in the audience shouted, hear, hear. All of us in the audience applauded, and I clapped pretty hard. Honestly, a department as warm as ours really is hard to find these days. A few days ago Xiao Li even said to me that if he ever gets promoted, he wants to lead people the same way.
